attacked.target: The receipt of 2,000 USDC is classified as income from the transfer of a virtual digital asset, taxed at 30% under s.115BBH. The value is determined on the settlement date (2026-06-23) using the telegraphic transfer buying rate. No TDS is required as the recipient is outside India. Under s.439(8), a bona fide disclosure of the income with all material facts is required to avoid penalties.
attacked.attack: The provision s.115BBH is incorrectly cited for the tax year FY 2026-27. The correct provision for the transfer of virtual digital assets should be verified for the stated tax year.
attacked.evidence: Section 115BBH, Income-tax Act, 1961 — carried into the Income-tax Act, 2025

attacked.attack: The provision s.115BBH does not reach the facts presented because USDC is defined as not being foreign currency according to s.2(47A)(a) of the Income-tax Act, 1961, which specifies that virtual digital assets are 'not being Indian currency or foreign currency.' Therefore, s.115BBH may not apply to USDC.
